10.8 Composition vs. Inheritance

# Composition (preferred): objects contain other objects
class RecordingDialog:
    def __init__(self, parent, project_dir, settings, store):
        self.settings = settings    # Has-a Settings
        self.store = store          # Has-a ModelStore
        self._worker = None        # Will have-a SynthesisWorker

# Inheritance (less common): is-a relationship
class DownloadPanel(wx.Panel):    # DownloadPanel IS-A wx.Panel
    def __init__(self, parent, store, downloader):
        super().__init__(parent)  # Call parent's __init__
        self.store = store

  11. Line 11: self.store = store
    Stores store in instance attribute store.
Prefer composition over inheritance. AIVS uses inheritance mainly for wxPython widgets (because wx requires it), and composition for everything else. Composition is more flexible and easier to test.

10.9 Key Takeaways

  • Classes define blueprints; objects are instances of classes
  • __init__ initializes new objects — it is NOT the constructor (the constructor is __new__)
  • self refers to the current instance — always the first parameter
  • Instance attributes are per-object; class attributes are shared
  • @property provides computed/validated attribute access
  • Dunder methods (__repr__, __eq__, __len__) make objects integrate with Python's built-in functions
  • Prefer composition — objects contain other objects rather than inheriting from them
  • The AIVS project has classes for every major subsystem: Settings, ModelStore, CloneClient, RecordingDialog, etc.
Exercise 10.1: Create a VoiceCatalog class that wraps the TTS catalog data. It should have methods: get_engines(), get_voices(engine_id), and find_voice(voice_id). Include __repr__ and __len__.

11.1 Inheritance Deep Dive

class BaseEngine:
    """Base class for all TTS engines."""
    sample_rate = 24000

    def __init__(self, voice_entry: dict):
        self.voice_entry = voice_entry

    def synthesize(self, text: str, speed: float = 1.0) -> "np.ndarray":
        raise NotImplementedError("Subclasses must implement synthesize")

    def close(self):
        pass  # Default: no cleanup needed

class SherpaEngine(BaseEngine):
    """sherpa-onnx based TTS engine."""
    def __init__(self, voice_entry: dict, model_files: dict):
        super().__init__(voice_entry)  # Call parent's __init__
        self.model_files = model_files
        self._model = None

    def synthesize(self, text, speed=1.0):
        if self._model is None:
            self._model = self._load_model()
        return self._model.generate(text, speed=speed)

class ClonedVoiceEngine(BaseEngine):
    """XTTS v2 voice cloning engine."""
    def __init__(self, voice_entry: dict, client: "CloneClient"):
        super().__init__(voice_entry)
        self._client = client
        self.sample_wav = voice_entry.get("sample")

    def synthesize(self, text, speed=1.0):
        return self._client.synthesize(text, self.sample_wav, speed=speed)

    def close(self):
        self._client.close()  # Override: shut down worker process

11.2 Abstract Base Classes

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod

class TtsEngine(ABC):
    """Abstract base class — cannot be instantiated directly."""

    sample_rate: int = 24000

    @abstractmethod
    def synthesize(self, text: str, sid: int = 0,
                    speed: float = 1.0, pitch: float = 1.0,
                    volume: float = 1.0) -> "np.ndarray":
        """Synthesize text to audio samples."""
        ...

    def close(self):
        """Clean up resources. Override if needed."""
        pass

# This will fail:
# engine = TtsEngine()  # TypeError: Can't instantiate abstract class

# Must implement all abstract methods
class MyEngine(TtsEngine):
    def synthesize(self, text, sid=0, speed=1.0, pitch=1.0, volume=1.0):
        # ... actual synthesis
        return np.zeros(100, dtype=np.int16)

11.3 Dataclasses

Dataclasses auto-generate __init__, __repr__, __eq__, and more:

from dataclasses import dataclass, field

@dataclass
class VoiceParams:
    """TTS voice parameters for a recording session."""
    rate: float = 1.0
    pitch: float = 1.0
    volume: float = 1.0
    compute: str = "auto"
    output_format: str = "wav"
    punctuation: str = "default"

# Auto-generated __init__
params = VoiceParams(rate=1.5, pitch=0.8)
print(params)  # VoiceParams(rate=1.5, pitch=0.8, volume=1.0, ...)

# Auto-generated __eq__
params2 = VoiceParams(rate=1.5, pitch=0.8)
print(params == params2)  # True

@dataclass(frozen=True)  # Immutable
class AudioConfig:
    sample_rate: int = 24000
    channels: int = 1
    sample_width: int = 2  # 16-bit = 2 bytes

# frozen=True makes it hashable (can be dict key or set member)
configs = {AudioConfig(): "default"}

@dataclass
class Segment:
    index: int
    title: str
    text: str
    status: str = "pending"
    saved: str | None = None
    duration: float = 0.0

    def is_done(self) -> bool:
        return self.status == "done" and self.saved is not None

11.4 Mixins

# Mixins provide reusable behavior
class LoggingMixin:
    """Adds a logger to any class."""
    @property
    def log(self):
        import logging
        return logging.getLogger(type(self).__name__)

class SingletonMixin:
    """Makes a class a singleton."""
    _instance = None
    _lock = threading.Lock()

    def __new__(cls, *args, **kwargs):
        if cls._instance is None:
            with cls._lock:
                if cls._instance is None:
                    cls._instance = super().__new__(cls)
        return cls._instance

# Usage
class AddonManager(SingletonMixin, LoggingMixin):
    def discover(self):
        self.log.info("Discovering addons...")

11.6 __slots__ for Memory Efficiency

class LightweightVoice:
    """Uses __slots__ to reduce memory per instance."""
    __slots__ = ("voice_id", "name", "sid")

    def __init__(self, voice_id, name, sid):
        self.voice_id = voice_id
        self.name = name
        self.sid = sid

# Cannot add arbitrary attributes
v = LightweightVoice("af", "AF", 0)
# v.extra = "data"  # AttributeError!

# Uses ~40% less memory than a regular class

11.7 Key Takeaways

  • Abstract base classes define interfaces that subclasses must implement
  • Dataclasses auto-generate boilerplate methods — use them for data containers
  • Mixins provide reusable behavior without deep inheritance hierarchies
  • super() should always be used — never hardcode parent class names
  • Enums represent fixed sets of values (compute modes, project types)
  • Composition over inheritance remains the golden rule

Ch12 Iterators
Chapter 12

Iterators & Generators

Learning Objectives

  • Understand the iterator protocol (__iter__ and __next__)
  • Create generator functions with yield
  • Use generator expressions for memory-efficient processing
  • Apply itertools for advanced iteration patterns

12.1 The Iterator Protocol

# Every iterable has __iter__ that returns an iterator
# Every iterator has __next__ that returns the next value

class VoiceIterator:
    """Iterates over voice entries in the catalog."""
    def __init__(self, catalog):
        self._catalog = catalog
        self._tts_idx = 0
        self._lang_idx = 0
        self._var_idx = 0
        self._voice_idx = 0

    def __iter__(self):
        return self  # Iterators return themselves

    def __next__(self):
        # Navigate through nested structure
        while self._tts_idx < len(self._catalog):
            tts = self._catalog[self._tts_idx]
            langs = tts.get("languages", [])
            while self._lang_idx < len(langs):
                lang = langs[self._lang_idx]
                variants = lang.get("variants", [])
                while self._var_idx < len(variants):
                    variant = variants[self._var_idx]
                    voices = variant.get("voices", [])
                    while self._voice_idx < len(voices):
                        voice = voices[self._voice_idx]
                        self._voice_idx += 1
                        return {"tts": tts["id"], "voice": voice}
                    self._var_idx += 1
                    self._voice_idx = 0
                self._lang_idx += 1
                self._var_idx = 0
            self._tts_idx += 1
            self._lang_idx = 0
        raise StopIteration

# Usage
for voice in VoiceIterator(catalog):
    print(voice)

12.2 Generator Functions

Generators use yield to produce values lazily, one at a time:

def voice_entries(catalog):
    """Yield all voice entries from the catalog (lazy)."""
    for tts in catalog:
        for lang in tts.get("languages", []):
            for variant in lang.get("variants", []):
                for voice in variant.get("voices", []):
                    yield {
                        "tts": tts["id"],
                        "language": lang["code"],
                        "variant": variant["id"],
                        "voice": voice,
                    }

# Usage — memory efficient (no list in memory)
for entry in voice_entries(catalog):
    print(entry["voice"]["id"])

# Can convert to list if needed
all_entries = list(voice_entries(catalog))

yield from — Delegating to Sub-generators

def all_paths(directory):
    """Recursively yield all file paths."""
    for entry in os.scandir(directory):
        if entry.is_file():
            yield entry.path
        elif entry.is_dir():
            yield from all_paths(entry.path)  # Delegate to sub-generator

12.3 Generator Expressions

# List comprehension creates list in memory
big_list = [x ** 2 for x in range(1_000_000)]  # ~8MB in memory

# Generator expression — lazy evaluation (almost no memory)
big_gen = (x ** 2 for x in range(1_000_000))  # One number at a time

# Common pattern: sum/count/min/max on generators
total_chars = sum(len(v["text"]) for v in segments)
max_length = max(len(s["text"]) for s in segments)
has_empty = any(not s["text"].strip() for s in segments)

12.4 itertools — Advanced Iteration

import itertools

# chain — concatenate iterables
all_voices = list(itertools.chain(piper_voices, kokoro_voices))

# islice — slice an iterator
first_10 = list(itertools.islice(voice_iterator, 10))

# groupby — group consecutive elements
from itertools import groupby
voices_sorted = sorted(voices, key=lambda v: v["tts"])
for tts_id, group in groupby(voices_sorted, key=lambda v: v["tts"]):
    print(f"{tts_id}: {len(list(group))} voices")

# product — Cartesian product
engines = ["piper", "kokoro"]
languages = ["en", "zh"]
for engine, lang in itertools.product(engines, languages):
    print(f"{engine}/{lang}")

# cycle — infinite cycling
spinner = itertools.cycle(["|", "/", "-", "\\"])
for _ in range(8):
    print(f"\r{next(spinner)} Loading...", end="")

12.5 Real Example: Segmented File Reading

# From AIVS: reading text files in chunks for large documents
def read_in_chunks(file_path: str, chunk_size: int = 4096):
    """Read a file in chunks — memory efficient."""
    with open(file_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        while True:
            chunk = f.read(chunk_size)
            if not chunk:
                break
            yield chunk

# Count words without loading entire file
def count_words(file_path: str) -> int:
    return sum(chunk.count(" ") + 1 for chunk in read_in_chunks(file_path))

    Returns the number of occurrences of a value.

12.6 Key Takeaways

  • Generators are the Pythonic way to create iterators — much simpler than implementing __iter__/__next__
  • yield pauses the function and produces a value; yield from delegates to sub-generators
  • Generators are lazy — they produce values on demand, saving memory
  • Generator expressions are like list comprehensions but with parentheses: (x for x in ...)
  • itertools provides powerful iteration building blocks (chain, groupby, product, etc.)

13.1 Function Basics — Functions Are Objects

# Functions are first-class objects in Python
def greet(name):
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

# Assign to a variable
say_hello = greet
print(say_hello("World"))  # "Hello, World!"

# Pass as argument
def apply(func, value):
    return func(value)

print(apply(greet, "Python"))  # "Hello, Python!"

# Return from another function
def make_greeting(greeting):
    def inner(name):
        return f"{greeting}, {name}!"
    return inner

hello = make_greeting("Hello")
hola = make_greeting("Hola")
print(hello("Alice"))  # "Hello, Alice!"
print(hola("Bob"))    # "Hola, Bob!"

13.2 Writing Your First Decorator

# A decorator is a function that takes a function and returns a new function
import functools

def timer(func):
    """Decorator that prints how long a function takes."""
    @functools.wraps(func)  # Preserves the original function's name/docstring
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        import time
        start = time.perf_counter()
        result = func(*args, **kwargs)
        elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start
        print(f"{func.__name__} took {elapsed:.3f}s")
        return result
    return wrapper

# Apply with @ syntax
@timer
def load_model(path):
    import time; time.sleep(0.1)  # Simulate loading
    return "model"

result = load_model("model.onnx")
# Output: load_model took 0.102s

# Equivalent without @ syntax
def load_model2(path):
    return "model"
load_model2 = timer(load_model2)

13.3 Decorators with Arguments

def retry(max_attempts=3, delay=1.0):
    """Decorator that retries a function on failure."""
    def decorator(func):
        @functools.wraps(func)
        def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
            for attempt in range(max_attempts):
                try:
                    return func(*args, **kwargs)
                except Exception as exc:
                    if attempt == max_attempts - 1:
                        raise
                    print(f"Attempt {attempt+1} failed, retrying...")
                    time.sleep(delay)
        return wrapper
    return decorator

@retry(max_attempts=5, delay=2.0)
def download_model(url):
    import requests
    return requests.get(url, timeout=30)

13.4 Common Built-in Decorators

class MyClass:
    # @property — computed attribute
    @property
    def display_name(self):
        return f"{self._name} v{self._version}"

    # @classmethod — receives class instead of instance
    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data: dict):
        return cls(data["name"], data["version"])

    # @staticmethod — no access to self or cls
    @staticmethod
    def is_valid(name: str) -> bool:
        return bool(name.strip())

# functools.lru_cache — memoization
@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=128)
def expensive_lookup(voice_id: str) -> dict:
    """Cache expensive database queries."""
    return db.query(voice_id)  # Only runs once per voice_id

# functools.cache (Python 3.9+) — unlimited cache
@functools.cache
def parse_version(version_str: str) -> tuple:
    return tuple(int(x) for x in version_str.split("."))

13.5 Decorator Patterns in AIVS

# The @property decorator pattern used throughout AIVS:
class Settings:
    @property
    def theme(self) -> str:
        return self._data.get("theme", "system")

    @property
    def compute(self) -> str:
        return self._data.get("compute", "auto")

# Context manager decorator pattern:
from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def busy_cursor():
    """Show busy cursor during an operation."""
    wx.BeginBusyCursor()
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        wx.EndBusyCursor()

13.6 Key Takeaways

  • A decorator is a function that wraps another function, modifying its behavior
  • Always use @functools.wraps(func) to preserve the original function's metadata
  • Decorators with arguments need three levels of nesting
  • Built-in decorators: @property, @classmethod, @staticmethod, @lru_cache
  • Decorators are used in AIVS for caching, timing, and GUI cursor management

Ch14 Context
Chapter 14

Context Managers

Learning Objectives

  • Understand the with statement and context manager protocol

14.1 The Context Manager Protocol

# Context managers implement __enter__ and __exit__
class ManagedEngine:
    """TTS engine that cleans up when done."""

    def __init__(self, engine_id: str):
        self.engine_id = engine_id
        self._model = None

    def __enter__(self):
        """Called when entering the 'with' block."""
        print(f"Loading {self.engine_id}...")
        self._model = "loaded"
        return self  # This is assigned to 'as' variable

    def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_val, exc_tb):
        """Called when exiting the 'with' block (always)."""
        print(f"Unloading {self.engine_id}...")
        self._model = None
        return False  # Don't suppress exceptions

# Usage
with ManagedEngine("piper") as engine:
    print(f"Using {engine.engine_id}")
    # ... use the engine ...
# "Unloading piper..." is printed here, even if an exception occurs

14.2 @contextmanager Decorator

from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def managed_engine(engine_id: str):
    """Simpler context manager using @contextmanager."""
    print(f"Loading {engine_id}...")
    engine = "loaded"
    try:
        yield engine  # This is the 'as' value
    finally:
        print(f"Unloading {engine_id}...")

# Usage (identical to the class version)
with managed_engine("piper") as engine:
    print(f"Using {engine}")

14.3 Context Managers in AIVS

# GUI busy cursor management
from contextlib import contextmanager

@contextmanager
def busy_cursor():
    """Show busy cursor during document parsing."""
    wx.BeginBusyCursor()
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        wx.EndBusyCursor()

# Usage in NewProjectWizard
with busy_cursor():
    doc = parse_document(self.source_path)
    segments = split_document(doc, mode)

# Thread-safe lock management
class CloneClient:
    def _request(self, req: dict) -> dict:
        with self._lock:  # Thread-safe access
            # ... send request and read response

# Temporary directory for downloads
import tempfile
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmpdir:
    # Download to tmpdir, process, then it's auto-cleaned
    download_to(tmpdir)

# contextlib.suppress — ignore specific exceptions
from contextlib import contextlib
with contextlib.suppress(FileNotFoundError):
    os.unlink(temp_file)  # Ignore if file doesn't exist

Regular Expressions

Learning Objectives

15.1 Regex Basics

import re

# Simple patterns
text = "Voice af_bella has sample rate 24000"

# re.search — find first match anywhere in string
match = re.search(r'\d+', text)
print(match.group())  # "24000"

# re.findall — find ALL matches as strings
numbers = re.findall(r'\d+', text)
print(numbers)  # ["24000"]

# re.match — match only at the START of string
match = re.match(r'Voice (\w+)', text)
print(match.group(1))  # "af_bella" (captured group)

# re.sub — substitute matches
clean = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', "too   many    spaces")
print(clean)  # "too many spaces"

15.2 Pattern Syntax

PatternMeaningExample
.Any characterr'h.t' → "hat", "hot"
\dDigit [0-9]r'\d\d' → "42"
\wWord char [a-zA-Z0-9_]r'\w+' → "hello"
\sWhitespacer'\s+' → " "
*Zero or morer'ab*c' → "ac", "abc"
+One or morer'ab+c' → "abc"
?Zero or oner'colou?r' → "color"
{n,m}n to m repetitionsr'\d{2,4}' → "12", "1234"
[abc]Character setr'[aeiou]' → vowels
[^abc]Negated setr'[^0-9]' → non-digits
|Alternation (or)r'cat|dog'
()Capture groupr'(\w+)@(\w+)'
(?:)Non-capturing groupr'(?:http|https)'
\bWord boundaryr'\bcat\b'
^Start of stringr'^Hello'
$End of stringr'\.txt$'

15.3 Common Patterns

# Validate file extension
def is_valid_docx(path: str) -> bool:
    return bool(re.match(r'\.docx$', path, re.IGNORECASE))

# Extract version numbers
text = "Version 2.0.1 (build 20260822)"
version = re.search(r'Version (\d+\.\d+\.\d+)', text)
print(version.group(1))  # "2.0.1"

# Split on multiple delimiters
parts = re.split(r'[;,\s]+', "Piper, Kokoro ; Matcha")
print(parts)  # ['Piper', 'Kokoro', 'Matcha']

# Clean up whitespace in text
text = "Too\n\n\nmany\n\nnewlines"
clean = re.sub(r'\n{3,}', '\n\n', text)

# Named groups
pattern = r'(?P<tts>\w+)/(?P<lang>\w+)/(?P<variant>\w+)'
match = re.match(pattern, "piper/en_US/medium")
if match:
    print(match.group("tts"))      # "piper"
    print(match.group("lang"))     # "en_US"
    print(match.group("variant"))  # "medium"

15.4 Regex in AIVS

# From util.py — filename sanitization
import re
def sanitize_filename(name: str, max_length: int = 80) -> str:
    name = re.sub(r'[<>:"/\\|?*]', '_', name)
    name = re.sub(r'\s+', ' ', name).strip()
    if len(name) > max_length:
        name = name[:max_length].rstrip()
    return name

# From documents/daisy_builder.py — DAISY ID sanitization
def _sanitize_id(text: str) -> str:
    s = re.sub(r"[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]", "_", text.lower())
    s = re.sub(r"_+", "_", s).strip("_")
    return s[:60] or "item"

# From documents/splitter.py — sentence splitting
def _split_sentences(text: str) -> list[str]:
    sentences = re.split(r'(?<=[.!?])\s+', text)
    return [s.strip() for s in sentences if s.strip()]

# Compiled patterns (faster for repeated use)
_FILE_EXT = re.compile(r'(\.\w+)$')
def get_extension(path: str) -> str:
    m = _FILE_EXT.search(path)
    return m.group(1) if m else ""

16.3 Time Performance Measurement

import time

# time.monotonic() — best for measuring elapsed time
start = time.monotonic()
# ... do work ...
elapsed = time.monotonic() - start
print(f"Elapsed: {elapsed:.3f}s")

# Used in AIVS server health check polling
def _wait_ready(self, timeout: float):
    """Poll health endpoint until server responds."""
    deadline = time.monotonic() + timeout
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        if self.health_check():
            return
        time.sleep(1.0)
    raise TimeoutError(f"Server not ready in {timeout}s")

# time.perf_counter() — highest resolution timer
start = time.perf_counter()
result = expensive_computation()
duration = time.perf_counter() - start

    A comment: <dc:date>2026-08-29T19:30:00Z</dc:date>.

16.5 Key Takeaways

  • datetime.now() for current time; timezone.utc for UTC
  • strftime() formats; strptime() parses
  • time.monotonic() for measuring elapsed time (not affected by clock changes)
  • AIVS uses ISO 8601 timestamps for DAISY book metadata

Ch17 Testing
Chapter 17

Testing with unittest & pytest

Learning Objectives

  • Write unit tests with unittest and pytest
  • Use assertions effectively
  • Understand test organization and naming conventions
  • See the AIVS test suite structure

17.1 Why Test?

AI Voice Studio has 99+ tests across 12 test files. Testing ensures:

  • Correctness — code does what it's supposed to
  • Regression prevention — changes don't break existing functionality
  • Documentation — tests show how code is intended to be used
  • Confidence — refactoring safely

17.2 unittest — The Standard Library

import unittest
from ai_voice_studio.util import sanitize_filename

class SanitizeFilenameTest(unittest.TestCase):
    """Tests for the sanitize_filename utility function."""

    def test_removes_illegal_characters(self):
        """Characters illegal on Windows should be replaced."""
        result = sanitize_filename('File: "Name" <bad>?')
        assert ":" not in result
        assert '"' not in result
        assert "<" not in result

    def test_truncates_long_names(self):
        """Names exceeding max_length should be truncated."""
        long_name = "A" * 200
        result = sanitize_filename(long_name, max_length=80)
        assert len(result) <= 80

    def test_strips_whitespace(self):
        """Leading/trailing whitespace should be removed."""
        result = sanitize_filename("  hello  ")
        assert result == "hello"

    def test_empty_name_returns_fallback(self):
        """Empty names should return a valid filename."""
        result = sanitize_filename("")
        assert result  # Non-empty

# Run with: python -m unittest tests/test_util.py

17.3 pytest — The Preferred Framework

# pytest tests are simpler — just use assert statements
from ai_voice_studio.tts import catalog

def test_tts_ids_are_unique():
    """Every TTS engine must have a unique ID."""
    ids = [t["id"] for t in catalog.get_tts_list()]
    assert len(ids) == len(set(ids))

def test_required_engines_present():
    """Piper, Kokoro, and Matcha must be in the catalog."""
    ids = {t["id"] for t in catalog.get_tts_list()}
    assert "piper" in ids
    assert "kokoro" in ids
    assert "matcha" in ids

def test_piper_voices_have_artifacts():
    """Every Piper voice must have a download artifact."""
    piper = catalog.find_tts("piper")
    assert piper is not None
    for lang in piper["languages"]:
        for variant in lang["variants"]:
            assert variant.get("artifact") or variant.get("voices")

# Run with: python -m pytest tests/ -v

17.4 Test Fixtures and Setup

import unittest
import tempfile
from unittest import mock

class ResolveVoiceFilesTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        """Called before each test method."""
        self.tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.models_root = os.path.join(self.tmp.name, "models")
        # Mock the paths module to use our temp directory
        self.patcher = mock.patch(
            "ai_voice_studio.paths.user_data_dir",
            return_value=self.tmp.name,
        )
        self.patcher.start()

    def tearDown(self):
        """Called after each test method."""
        self.patcher.stop()
        self.tmp.cleanup()

    def _voice_dir(self, name: str) -> str:
        """Create a voice directory in the temp area."""
        d = os.path.join(self.models_root, name)
        os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
        return d

    def test_matcha_finds_acoustic_model(self):
        vdir = self._voice_dir("matcha_en/default")
        open(os.path.join(vdir, "model-steps-3.onnx"), "w").close()
        open(os.path.join(vdir, "tokens.txt"), "w").close()
        # ... test resolve_voice_files finds the right files

Ch18 Json Xml

JSON, XML & Structured Data

Learning Objectives

18.1 JSON in Depth

import json

# Python ↔ JSON type mapping
# dict    →  object
# list    →  array
# str     →  string
# int/float → number
# True    →  true
# False   →  false
# None    →  null

# Complex serialization
data = {
    "name": "My Project",
    "segments": [
        {"index": 1, "title": "Chapter 1", "text": "..."},
        {"index": 2, "title": "Chapter 2", "text": "..."},
    ],
    "tts": {
        "voice": "af_bella",
        "rate": 1.0,
        "pitch": 1.0,
    },
}

# Serialize with nice formatting
json_str = json.dumps(data, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
print(json_str)

# Deserialize
loaded = json.loads(json_str)

# Write to file
with open("project.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    json.dump(data, f, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

# Read from file
with open("project.json", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    loaded = json.load(f)

3. TTS Worker Protocol

# JSON lines protocol between app and worker subprocesses
# Request (app → worker):
{"cmd": "synthesize", "text": "Hello world", "speed": 1.0}
# Response (worker → app):
{"ok": true, "wav": "base64-encoded-audio..."}

# Error response:

18.3 XML Basics (for DAISY)

# AIVS generates XML for DAISY 2.02 books
# NCC.html (Navigation Center Combined)
ncc = f"""<!DOCTYPE html PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD XHTML 1.0 Transitional//EN"
  "http://www.w3.org/TR/xhtml1/DTD/xhtml1-transitional.dtd">
<html xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1999/xhtml" xml:lang="en" lang="en">
<head>
  <title>{title}</title>
  <meta name="dc:title" content="{title}" />
  <meta name="dc:identifier" content="{book_uid}" />
</head>
<body>
  <h1>{title}</h1>
  <h2><a href="Chapter_1.smil">Chapter 1</a></h2>
</body>
</html>"""

opf = """<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

    <dc:title>{title}</dc:title>
    <dc:identifier>{uid}</dc:identifier>
    <dc:language>{lang}</dc:language>

</package>"""

  <body>
    <seq>
      <par>

</smil>"""

18.4 Structured Data Patterns

# Pattern: Default dict with deep merge
def deep_merge(base: dict, override: dict) -> dict:
    """Merge two dicts, with override taking precedence."""
    result = dict(base)
    for key, value in override.items():
        if key in result and isinstance(result[key], dict) and isinstance(value, dict):
            result[key] = deep_merge(result[key], value)
        else:
            result[key] = value
    return result

# Pattern: Typed dict for structured data
from typing import TypedDict

class SegmentDict(TypedDict, total=False):
    index: int
    title: str
    text: str
    status: str
    saved: str
    duration: float

18.5 Key Takeaways

  • JSON is the primary data format in AIVS — settings, projects, and worker protocols all use it
  • json.dumps/loads for strings; json.dump/load for files
  • Always use ensure_ascii=False for Unicode text
  • XML is used for DAISY 2.02 book structure (NCC, OPF, SMIL files)
  • The worker protocol uses JSON lines (one JSON object per line)

Ch19 Concurrency
Part III

Advanced Python

Chapter 19

Concurrency & Threading

Learning Objectives

  • Understand the GIL (Global Interpreter Lock) and its implications
  • Use threading for I/O-bound concurrency
  • Synchronize access with locks, events, and conditions
  • See threading patterns in AIVS (background TTS, downloads)

19.1 The GIL and When to Use Threads

Python's GIL (Global Interpreter Lock) means only one thread executes Python bytecode at a time. This makes threads unsuitable for CPU-bound work but excellent for I/O-bound tasks:

Task TypeSolutionAIVS Example
I/O-bound (network, disk)threadingDownloading models, file I/O
CPU-bound (computation)multiprocessingN/A (use subprocesses instead)
GUI + background workthreadingTTS synthesis + UI updates

19.2 Basic Threading

import threading

# Simple thread
def download_model(url, dest):
    import time
    time.sleep(2)  # Simulate download
    print(f"Downloaded to {dest}")

t = threading.Thread(target=download_model, args=("http://...", "/tmp/model"))
t.start()   # Starts in background
t.join()    # Wait for completion

# Daemon thread (dies when main program exits)
t = threading.Thread(target=background_task, daemon=True)
t.start()
# No need to join — it dies with the main thread

19.3 Thread Synchronization

import threading

# Lock — mutual exclusion
_lock = threading.Lock()

def thread_safe_operation():
    with _lock:
        # Only one thread can execute this block at a time
        critical_section()

# RLock — reentrant lock (same thread can acquire multiple times)
_rlock = threading.RLock()

# Event — signaling between threads
cancel_event = threading.Event()

def worker():
    while not cancel_event.is_set():
        # Do work...
        if cancel_event.is_set():
            break  # Check between each segment

# Usage in AIVS — cancel a download
cancel_event = threading.Event()
t = threading.Thread(target=download, args=(url, dest, cancel_event))
t.start()

# User clicks Cancel
cancel_event.set()  # Signal the thread to stop
t.join()

19.4 Threading in AIVS

The Synthesis Worker Pattern

# From jobs/synthesizer.py — background TTS processing
class SynthesisWorker(threading.Thread):
    """Background thread that synthesizes audio segments."""

    def __init__(self, segments, voice_entry, params,
                 output_dir, on_segment_done, on_all_done,
                 on_error, cancel_event, pause_event, on_status):
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self._segments = segments
        self._voice_entry = voice_entry
        self._cancel = cancel_event
        self._pause = pause_event
        self._on_done = on_segment_done
        self._on_all_done = on_all_done
        self._on_error = on_error
        self._on_status = on_status
        self._output_dir = output_dir

    def run(self):
        """Main thread loop — runs in background thread."""
        try:
            engine = get_engine(self._voice_entry)
            for i, seg in enumerate(self._segments):
                # Check for cancellation
                if self._cancel.is_set():
                    break

                # Check for pause
                while self._pause.is_set():
                    if self._cancel.is_set():
                        break
                    time.sleep(0.1)

                # Synthesize
                self._on_status(f"Recording segment {i+1}...")
                audio = engine.synthesize(
                    seg.text,
                    speed=self._params["rate"],
                    pitch=self._params["pitch"],
                    volume=self._params["volume"],
                )

                # Save to disk immediately
                path = self._save_audio(seg, audio)

                # Notify GUI (thread-safe via wx.PostEvent)
                self._on_done(i, seg.title, path)

            self._on_all_done()
        except Exception as exc:
            self._on_error(str(exc))

    def cancel(self):
        self._cancel.set()

    def pause(self):
        self._pause.set()

    def resume(self):
        self._pause.clear()

Thread-Safe GUI Communication

# wxPython requires UI updates on the main thread
# Workers post events, GUI handles them on the main thread

# From gui/events.py
_SYNTH_STATUS = wx.NewEventType()
EVT_SYNTH_STATUS = wx.PyEventBinder(_SYNTH_STATUS, 1)

class SynthStatusEvent(wx.PyCommandEvent):
    def __init__(self, message: str):
        super().__init__(_SYNTH_STATUS)
        self.message = message

# In the worker thread:
def _on_status(self, msg):
    wx.PostEvent(self, SynthStatusEvent(msg))

# In the GUI (main thread):
self.Bind(EVT_SYNTH_STATUS, self._handle_status)

def _handle_status(self, evt: SynthStatusEvent):
    self.status_label.SetLabel(evt.message)  # Safe — on main thread

19.5 Download Threading Pattern

# From gui/model_panels.py — background download
def _on_download(self, _):
    self._cancel_event = threading.Event()
    self._thread = threading.Thread(
        target=self._download_job,
        args=(tts_id, lang_code, variants),
        daemon=True,
    )
    self._thread.start()

def _download_job(self, tts_id, lang_code, variants):
    def progress(name, done, total):
        wx.PostEvent(self, DownloadProgressEvent(name, done, total))

    try:
        for variant_id in variants:
            self.downloader.download_variant(
                tts_id, lang_code, variant_id,
                progress=progress,
                cancel_event=self._cancel_event,
            )
        wx.PostEvent(self, DownloadFinishedEvent(True, "Done!"))
    except DownloadCancelled:
        wx.PostEvent(self, DownloadFinishedEvent(False, "Cancelled"))
    except Exception as exc:
        wx.PostEvent(self, DownloadFinishedEvent(False, str(exc)))

19.6 Key Takeaways

  • The GIL limits true parallelism in threads — use threads for I/O, not CPU work
  • threading.Thread creates background threads; always use daemon=True for non-critical threads
  • threading.Event is the primary mechanism for cancellation in AIVS
  • wx.PostEvent() is the only safe way to update GUI from worker threads
  • The AIVS SynthesisWorker pattern: thread + cancel event + pause event + GUI events
Exercise 19.1: Create a simple download simulator using threads. It should download 5 files concurrently, report progress via events, and support cancellation.

FeatureThreadsProcesses

20.2 The subprocess Module

import subprocess

# Run a command and wait
result = subprocess.run(
    ["python", "-c", "print('hello')"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
)
print(result.stdout)       # "hello\n"
print(result.returncode)   # 0

# Start a long-running process
proc = subprocess.Popen(
    ["python", "-m", "worker"],
    stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
    stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
    text=True,
)

# Communicate via stdin/stdout
proc.stdin.write('{"cmd": "ping"}\n')
proc.stdin.flush()
response = proc.stdout.readline()  # Read one line

# Terminate
proc.terminate()
proc.wait(timeout=5)

20.3 AIVS Subprocess Architecture

AI Voice Studio uses subprocesses to isolate heavy runtimes (PyTorch, ONNX) from the main GUI process. This is a critical architectural decision: 

# From clone/__init__.py — CloneClient manages a subprocess
class CloneClient:
    def _ensure_proc(self):
        if self._proc is not None and self._proc.poll() is None:
            return
        cmd = [sys.executable, "-m", "ai_voice_studio.clone.worker"]
        self._proc = subprocess.Popen(
            cmd,
            stdin=subprocess.PIPE,
            stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
            stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,
            text=True,
            bufsize=1,
        )
        # Verify the worker started
        resp = self._request({"cmd": "ping"})
        if not resp.get("ok"):
            raise CloneEngineError("Worker failed to start")

    def _request(self, req: dict) -> dict:
        """Send JSON request, read JSON response."""
        with self._lock:
            req["id"] = self._next_id
            self._next_id += 1
            self._proc.stdin.write(json.dumps(req) + "\n")
            self._proc.stdin.flush()
            line = self._proc.stdout.readline()
            return json.loads(line)

# Protocol: JSON lines over stdin/stdout
# Request:  {"cmd": "synthesize", "text": "Hello", "speed": 1.0}
# Response: {"ok": true, "wav": "base64..."}

20.5 Key Takeaways

  • Use subprocess when you need true isolation (different runtime, memory space)
  • AIVS uses subprocesses for TTS engines to prevent runtime conflicts
  • JSON lines protocol over stdin/stdout is the communication pattern
  • Always use threading.RLock to synchronize access to the subprocess

Ch21 Async
Chapter 21

Async I/O

Learning Objectives

  • Understand asyncio's event loop model
  • Write async functions with async/await
  • Understand when async is appropriate vs. threads
  • See where AIVS could benefit from async patterns

21.1 What Is Async I/O?

asyncio is Python's built-in framework for writing concurrent code using coroutines. Unlike threads, async code runs in a single thread and cooperatively yields control at await points.

FeatureThreadsAsync
ParallelismPreemptive (GIL)Cooperative (single thread)
OverheadPer-thread stack (~8MB)Per-coroutine (~KB)
Best forMixed I/O + some CPUHigh-concurrency I/O
GUI compatible?Yes (PostEvent)Needs event loop integration

21.2 Async Basics

import asyncio

# Define a coroutine
async def fetch_model(url: str) -> bytes:
    import aiohttp
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
        async with session.get(url) as response:
            return await response.read()

# Run a coroutine
data = asyncio.run(fetch_model("https://example.com/model.onnx"))

# Multiple concurrent coroutines
async def download_all(urls: list[str]):
    tasks = [fetch_model(url) for url in urls]
    results = await asyncio.gather(*tasks)
    return results

    Imports the asyncio module.

    A comment: Define a coroutine.

    Defines an asynchronous function (coroutine). Can use 'await' inside.
  4. Line 4: import aiohttp
    Imports the aiohttp module.
  5. Line 5: async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
    async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session:
  6. Line 6: async with session.get(url) as response:
    Returns the value for a key, or a default value if the key doesn't exist. Safer than direct access.
  7. Line 7: return await response.read()
    Reads the entire file contents as a string.

    A comment: Run a coroutine.

    Runs an async function in the event loop. Entry point for async programs.
  10. Line 10: # Multiple concurrent coroutines

    Assigns [fetch_model(url) for url in urls] to tasks.

  14. Line 14: return results
    Returns results to the caller.

21.3 When Async Isn't the Right Choice

AI Voice Studio uses threads, not async, because:

  • wxPython is not async-compatible — its event loop conflicts with asyncio
  • Blocking libraries — sherpa-onnx and NumPy are synchronous
  • Subprocess isolation — heavy work runs in separate processes anyway
  • Thread simplicity — for 5-10 concurrent tasks, threads are simpler
When to use async: Web servers handling thousands of connections, web scrapers, WebSocket clients. For a desktop app with a handful of background tasks, threads are the better choice.

21.4 Key Takeaways

  • async/await is for I/O-bound concurrency in a single thread
  • asyncio.gather() runs multiple coroutines concurrently
  • AIVS uses threads + subprocesses instead, because wxPython and ML libraries are synchronous
  • Async shines for high-concurrency network I/O (hundreds of connections)

Ch22 Type Hints
Chapter 22

Type Hints & Static Typing

Learning Objectives

  • Understand type hints and their benefits
  • Use modern type hint syntax (Python 3.9-3.12)
  • See type hints throughout the AIVS codebase

22.1 Why Type Hints?

Type hints document expected types without enforcing them at runtime. Benefits:

  • IDE support — autocompletion, error detection
  • Documentation — function signatures are self-documenting
  • Catch bugs early — static type checkers (mypy, Pylance) catch type errors before runtime
  • Refactoring safety — rename a method and see all affected call sites

22.2 Basic Type Hints

# Variable annotations
name: str = "AI Voice Studio"
version: float = 2.0
voices: list[str] = ["af", "am_adam"]

# Function annotations
def greet(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}!"

# No return value (returns None)
def log(message: str) -> None:
    print(message)

# Optional values
def find(items: list, index: int) -> str | None:
    if 0 <= index < len(items):
        return items[index]
    return None

    def __init__(self, children: list["Node"] | None = None):
        self.children = children or []

# Or use from __future__ import annotations (Python 3.7+)
from __future__ import annotations  # All annotations are strings by default

class Node:
    def __init__(self, children: list[Node] | None = None):
        self.children = children or  # No quotes needed!

22.6 Key Takeaways

  • Type hints are optional documentation that help IDEs and catch bugs
  • Use Python 3.10+ syntax: str | None instead of Optional[str]
  • TypedDict for structured dicts, Callable for function types
  • AIVS uses type hints on all public function signatures
  • from __future__ import annotations enables forward references

23.1 How Python Creates Classes

MyClass = type("MyClass", (), {"x": 42})
print(MyClass().x)  # 42

23.2 Custom Metaclasses

class AutoRegisterMeta(type):
    """Automatically register subclasses."""
    _registry: dict[str, type] = {}

    def __new__(mcs, name, bases, namespace):
        cls = super().__new__(mcs, name, bases, namespace)
        if bases:  # Don't register the base class itself
            mcs._registry[name] = cls
        return cls

class Engine(metaclass=AutoRegisterMeta):
    pass

class PiperEngine(Engine):
    pass  # Auto-registered!

class KokoroEngine(Engine):
    pass  # Auto-registered!

print(AutoRegisterMeta._registry)
# {'PiperEngine': <class 'PiperEngine'>, 'KokoroEngine': <class 'KokoroEngine'>}

23.3 Descriptors

Descriptors are objects that define __get__, __set__, or __delete__. They power @property:

class Validated:
    """Descriptor that validates values on assignment."""

    def __init__(self, min_val: float, max_val: float):
        self.min_val = min_val
        self.max_val = max_val

    def __set_name__(self, owner, name):
        self.name = name

    def __get__(self, obj, objtype=None):
        if obj is None:
            return self
        return obj.__dict__.get(self.name, 1.0)

    def __set__(self, obj, value):
        if not (self.min_val <= value <= self.max_val):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{self.name} must be between {self.min_val} and {self.max_val}"
            )
        obj.__dict__[self.name] = value

class VoiceParams:
    rate = Validated(0.5, 2.0)
    pitch = Validated(0.5, 2.0)
    volume = Validated(0.0, 2.0)

params = VoiceParams()
params.rate = 1.5   # OK
# params.rate = 5.0  # ValueError!

23.4 Key Takeaways

  • Metaclasses customize class creation — powerful but rarely needed
  • Descriptors power @property and can add validation, caching, etc.

24.1 Singleton Pattern

# Ensures only one instance exists
class Settings:
    _instance = None
    _lock = threading.Lock()

    def __new__(cls, *args, **kwargs):
        if cls._instance is None:
            with cls._lock:
                if cls._instance is None:
                    cls._instance = super().__new__(cls)
        return cls._instance

# From AIVS — the addon manager is a singleton
_default_manager: AddonManager | None = None
_manager_lock = threading.Lock()

def get_addon_manager() -> AddonManager:
    global _default_manager
    if _default_manager is None:
        with _manager_lock:
            if _default_manager is None:
                _default_manager = AddonManager()
    return _default_manager

  3. Line 3: _instance = None
    Assigns None to _instance.
  4. Line 4: _lock = threading.Lock()
    A mutual exclusion lock. Only one thread can hold it at a time. Prevents race conditions.

24.2 Observer Pattern

# wxPython events ARE the observer pattern
# Custom events notify the GUI of background changes

# From gui/events.py
_DOWNLOAD_PROGRESS = wx.NewEventType()
EVT_DOWNLOAD_PROGRESS = wx.PyEventBinder(_DOWNLOAD_PROGRESS, 1)

class DownloadProgressEvent(wx.PyCommandEvent):
    def __init__(self, name: str, done: int, total: int):
        super().__init__(_DOWNLOAD_PROGRESS)
        self.name = name
        self.done = done
        self.total = total

# Observer (worker thread) posts events:
wx.PostEvent(self, DownloadProgressEvent(name, 50, 100))

# Subscriber (GUI) handles events:
self.Bind(EVT_DOWNLOAD_PROGRESS, self._on_progress)

def _on_progress(self, evt):
    self.gauge.SetValue(evt.done * 100 // evt.total)

24.3 Strategy Pattern

# Different document parsers for different file types
class Parser(Protocol):
    def parse(self, path: str) -> Document: ...

class PdfParser:
    def parse(self, path): ...

class DocxParser:
    def parse(self, path): ...

# Strategy selection at runtime
parsers = {
    ".pdf": PdfParser(),
    ".docx": DocxParser(),
}

def parse_document(path: str) -> Document:
    ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower()
    parser = parsers.get(ext)
    if parser is None:
        raise ParseError(f"Unsupported: {ext}")
    return parser.parse(path)

24.4 Factory Pattern

# From tts/engine.py — factory that creates the right engine
def get_engine(voice_entry: dict) -> TtsEngine:
    """Factory: create the appropriate engine for a voice."""
    engine_type = voice_entry.get("engine", "vits")

    if engine_type == "xtts":
        client = CloneClient()
        return XtTsCloneEngine(voice_entry, client)
    elif engine_type == "omnivoice":
        return OmniVoiceEngine(voice_entry)
    elif engine_type == "omnivoice_server":
        return OmniVoiceServerEngine(voice_entry)
    else:
        return SherpaEngine(voice_entry)  # Default: sherpa-onnx

25.2 Introspection in the Addon System

# From addons/__init__.py — dynamic module loading
import importlib.util

def _register_engine(self, manifest, addon_dir):
    """Import and cache the addon's engine class."""
    module_name, class_name = manifest.engine_entry_point.split(":")
    full_path = os.path.join(addon_dir, module_name + ".py")

    # Dynamic import from file
    spec = importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(
        f"_aivs_engine_{manifest.engine_id}",
        full_path,
    )
    if spec and spec.loader:
        module = importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec)
        sys.modules[f"_aivs_engine_{manifest.engine_id}"] = module
        spec.loader.exec_module(module)

        # Get class by name (introspection)
        engine_class = getattr(module, class_name, None)
        if engine_class:
            self._engines[manifest.engine_id] = {
                "class": engine_class,
                "manifest": manifest,

26.1 ctypes Basics

import ctypes

# Load a shared library
libc = ctypes.CDLL("libc.so.6")  # Linux
# libc = ctypes.CDLL("msvcrt.dll")  # Windows

# Call C functions
libc.printf(b"Hello from C!\n")

# Type mapping
ctypes.c_int(42)        # C int
ctypes.c_double(3.14)   # C double
ctypes.c_char_p(b"hi")  # C char*
ctypes.c_bool(True)     # C bool

26.2 How sherpa-onnx Works

# sherpa-onnx is a Python package wrapping C++ ONNX inference
# AIVS accesses it like any Python library:
import sherpa_onnx

# Create TTS config
config = sherpa_onnx.OfflineTtsConfig(
    model=sherpa_onnx.OfflineTtsModelConfig(
        vits=sherpa_onnx.OfflineTtsVitsModelConfig(
            model="model.onnx",
            tokens="tokens.txt",
            data_dir="espeak-ng-data",
        ),
    ),
)

# Create engine and synthesize
tts = sherpa_onnx.OfflineTts(config)
audio = tts.generate(text="Hello world", sid=0, speed=1.0)

# audio.samples is a numpy array
import numpy as np
samples = np.array(audio.samples, dtype=np.int16)

26.3 NumPy and C

# NumPy arrays are stored as C arrays in memory
import numpy as np

arr = np.array([1, 2, 3, 4], dtype=np.int16)

# Access the C pointer
ptr = arr.ctypes.data  # Memory address
print(f"Array at {ptr}, {arr.shape} elements of {arr.dtype}")

# This is how audio data flows through the system:
# sherpa-onnx → C++ inference → numpy array → wxPython playback

27.1 What Is wxPython?

wxPython is a Python wrapper around the wxWidgets C++ GUI toolkit. It provides native-looking widgets on each platform — Windows controls look like Windows controls, macOS controls look like macOS controls, etc.

FeaturewxPythonTkinterPyQt
Native look?Yes (wraps native widgets)No (custom rendering)Mostly
LicensewxWindows (permissive)PSF (Python)GPL/Commercial
AccessibilityGood (MSAA/UIA on Windows)BasicGood
Learning curveModerateEasySteep

27.2 Hello wxPython

import wx

class MyFrame(wx.Frame):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__(
            None,
            title="Hello wxPython",
            size=(400, 300),
        )
        panel = wx.Panel(self)
        label = wx.StaticText(panel, label="Hello, World!")
        sizer = wx.BoxSizer(wx.VERTICAL)
        sizer.Add(label, 0, wx.ALL, 20)
        panel.SetSizer(sizer)

# Application entry point
app = wx.App(False)
frame = MyFrame()
frame.Show()
app.MainLoop()

27.4 The AIVS MainFrame

# From gui/main_frame.py
class MainFrame(wx.Frame):
    def __init__(self, parent, settings: Settings, store: ModelStore):
        super().__init__(
            parent,
            title=f"{APP_NAME} v{APP_VERSION}",
            size=(800, 600),
        )
        self.settings = settings
        self.store = store

        self._build_menu()
        self._build_ui()
        self._bind_events()

        self.Centre()
        self.SetStatusText("Ready")

    def _build_menu(self):
        """Build the menu bar with File, Edit, Tools, Settings, Help."""
        menubar = wx.MenuBar()

        # File menu
        file_menu = wx.Menu()
        file_menu.Append(ID_NEW_PROJECT, "&New Project\tCtrl+Shift+N")
        file_menu.Append(ID_OPEN_PROJECT, "&Open Project\tCtrl+O")
        file_menu.AppendSeparator()
        file_menu.Append(wx.ID_EXIT, "E&xit\tAlt+F4")
        menubar.Append(file_menu, "&File")

        # Tools menu
        tools_menu = wx.Menu()
        tools_menu.Append(ID_RECORD, "&Record\tCtrl+Shift+R")
        menubar.Append(tools_menu, "&Tools")

        # Settings menu
        settings_menu = wx.Menu()
        settings_menu.Append(ID_SETTINGS, "&Settings\tCtrl+,")
        menubar.Append(settings_menu, "&Settings")

        self.SetMenuBar(menubar)

Ch28 Sizers Layout
Chapter 28

Sizers & Layout

Learning Objectives

  • Understand wxPython's layout system (sizers)
  • Use BoxSizer, FlexGridSizer, and GridSizer
  • See layout patterns in AIVS dialogs

28.1 Why Sizers?

wxPython does not use absolute positioning. Instead, sizers automatically arrange widgets, handling resizing, padding, and alignment.

28.2 BoxSizer — The Most Common

# Vertical layout (widgets stack top to bottom)
sizer = wx.BoxSizer(wx.VERTICAL)
sizer.Add(label, 0, wx.ALL, 10)       # 0 = don't expand
sizer.Add(text_ctrl, 1, wx.EXPAND | wx.ALL, 5)  # 1 = expand proportionally
sizer.Add(button, 0, wx.ALIGN_RIGHT | wx.ALL, 5)

# Horizontal layout (widgets go left to right)
hbox = wx.BoxSizer(wx.HORIZONTAL)
hbox.Add(start_btn, 0, wx.ALL, 4)
hbox.Add(pause_btn, 0, wx.ALL, 4)
hbox.Add(stop_btn, 0, wx.ALL, 4)

# Add with proportion, flags, and border
sizer.Add(
    widget,

FlagMeaning

28.4 Layout in AIVS Recording Dialog

# From recording_dialog.py — nested sizer layout
def _build_ui(self):
    sizer = wx.BoxSizer(wx.VERTICAL)

    # Title
    title = wx.StaticText(self, label=f"Project: {title_text}")
    sizer.Add(title, 0, wx.ALL, 6)

    # Text preview
    self.text_preview = wx.TextCtrl(
        self, style=wx.TE_MULTILINE | wx.TE_READONLY, size=(-1, 130),
    )
    sizer.Add(self.text_preview, 0, wx.EXPAND | wx.LEFT | wx.RIGHT, 6)

    # Model selectors (grid layout)
    grid = wx.FlexGridSizer(cols=2, vgap=6, hgap=8)
    grid.AddGrowableCol(1)
    add_labeled(self, grid, "TTS engine", self.tts_combo)
    add_labeled(self, grid, "Language", self.lang_combo)
    add_labeled(self, grid, "Voice", self.voice_combo)
    sizer.Add(grid, 0, wx.EXPAND | wx.ALL, 6)

    # Buttons (horizontal)
    btns = wx.BoxSizer(wx.HORIZONTAL)
    btns.Add(self.start_btn, 0, wx.ALL, 4)
    btns.Add(self.pause_btn, 0, wx.ALL, 4)
    btns.Add(self.stop_btn, 0, wx.ALL, 4)
    sizer.Add(btns, 0, wx.LEFT, 2)

    # Progress bar (expands horizontally)
    self.gauge = wx.Gauge(self, range=100, size=(-1, 22))
    sizer.Add(self.gauge, 0, wx.EXPAND | wx.ALL, 6)

    self.SetSizer(sizer)

28.5 Key Takeaways

  • BoxSizer for linear layouts (vertical/horizontal)
  • FlexGridSizer for form-style layouts (label + control pairs)
  • Proportion controls how space is shared (0 = fixed, 1+ = proportional)
  • Flags control alignment, expansion, and borders
  • Nest sizers for complex layouts

29.2 The add_labeled Helper (AIVS)

# From gui/a11y.py — reusable helper for label+control pairs
def add_labeled(parent, sizer, label_text, control, **kwargs):
    """Add a label-control pair to a sizer."""
    label = wx.StaticText(parent, label=label_text + ":")
    control.SetName(label_text)  # Accessibility name
    sizer.Add(label, 0, wx.ALIGN_CENTER_VERTICAL | wx.ALL, 4)
    sizer.Add(control, 1, wx.EXPAND | wx.ALL, 4)
    return label

# Usage
add_labeled(self, grid, "TTS engine", self.tts_combo)
add_labeled(self, grid, "Language", self.lang_combo)

29.3 Slider with Value Display

# From recording_dialog.py — slider with live value label
def _slider(self, grid, name: str, lo: float, hi: float) -> wx.Slider:
    label = wx.StaticText(self, label=name + ":")
    slider = wx.Slider(
        self,
        minValue=int(lo * 100),
        maxValue=int(hi * 100),
        value=int(1.0 * 100),
    )
    value_label = wx.StaticText(self, label="1.00")
    slider.value_label = value_label  # Attach label to slider

    # Update label when slider moves
    slider.Bind(
        wx.EVT_SLIDER,
        lambda evt, s=slider, vl=value_label, n=name: (
            vl.SetLabel(f"{s.GetValue() / 100.0:.2f}"),
            s.SetName(f"{n}: {s.GetValue() / 100.0:.2f}"),
        ),
    )

    box = wx.BoxSizer(wx.HORIZONTAL)
    box.Add(slider, 1, wx.EXPAND)
    box.Add(value_label, 0, wx.LEFT | wx.ALIGN_CENTER_VERTICAL, 6)
    grid.Add(label, 0, wx.ALIGN_CENTER_VERTICAL)
    grid.Add(box, 1, wx.EXPAND)
    return slider

29.4 Key Takeaways

30.2 Custom Events (Worker → GUI)

# From gui/events.py
# Step 1: Create a unique event type
_SYNTH_STATUS = wx.NewEventType()
EVT_SYNTH_STATUS = wx.PyEventBinder(_SYNTH_STATUS, 1)

# Step 2: Create an event class
class SynthStatusEvent(wx.PyCommandEvent):
    def __init__(self, message: str):
        super().__init__(_SYNTH_STATUS)
        self.message = message

# Step 3: Post from worker thread
def _on_status(self, msg):
    wx.PostEvent(self, SynthStatusEvent(msg))

# Step 4: Handle in GUI (main thread)
self.Bind(EVT_SYNTH_STATUS, self._handle_status)

def _handle_status(self, evt: SynthStatusEvent):
    self.status_label.SetLabel(evt.message)

EventPurposePosted From
SynthStatusEventStatus update messageSynthesisWorker

30.3 Event Propagation

# Events propagate up the widget hierarchy
# Use evt.Skip() to let parent handle the event too

def _on_close(self, evt):
    if self._worker and self._worker.is_alive():
        answer = wx.MessageBox(
            "Recording is running. Stop and close?",
            "Close",
            style=wx.YES_NO | wx.ICON_QUESTION,
        )
        if answer != wx.YES:
            return  # Don't close — consume the event
        self._worker.cancel()
    self._save_tts_to_project()
    self.EndModal(wx.ID_CLOSE)

30.4 Key Takeaways

  • Bind() connects events to handler methods
  • wx.PostEvent() is the only safe way to send events from worker threads
  • Custom events use NewEventType() + PyEventBinder()

31.1 Modal Dialogs

# wx.Dialog — blocks the parent until closed
class MyDialog(wx.Dialog):
    def __init__(self, parent):
        super().__init__(parent, title="Settings", size=(600, 400))
        panel = wx.Panel(self)
        sizer = wx.BoxSizer(wx.VERTICAL)
        sizer.Add(wx.StaticText(panel, label="Configure settings here"))
        ok_btn = wx.Button(panel, wx.ID_OK, label="Save")
        cancel_btn = wx.Button(panel, wx.ID_CANCEL, label="Cancel")
        btn_sizer = wx.BoxSizer(wx.HORIZONTAL)
        btn_sizer.Add(ok_btn, 0, wx.ALL, 5)
        btn_sizer.Add(cancel_btn, 0, wx.ALL, 5)
        sizer.Add(btn_sizer)
        panel.SetSizer(sizer)

# Show modal dialog
dlg = MyDialog(self)
result = dlg.ShowModal()  # Blocks until closed
if result == wx.ID_OK:
    # User clicked Save
    pass
dlg.Destroy()  # Always destroy after use

from wx.adv import Wizard, WizardPage

class NewProjectWizard(Wizard):
    def __init__(self, parent, settings, store):
        super().__init__(parent, title="New Project - AI Voice Studio")

        # Page 1: project details
        self.page_details = _DetailsPage(self)
        self.page_details.name_ctrl = wx.TextCtrl(...)
        self.page_details.open_btn = wx.Button(...)

        # Page 2: audio mode selection
        self.page_mode = _ModePage(self, settings)
        self.page_mode.radios = [...]
        self.page_mode.description = wx.StaticText(...)

        self.GetPageAreaSizer().Add(self.page_details)

        self.Bind(EVT_WIZARD_FINISHED, self._on_finish)

    def _on_finish(self, _):
        """Called when user clicks Finish."""
        name = self.page_details.name_ctrl.GetValue().strip()
        mode = self.page_mode.selected()

        # Parse document and create project
        doc = parse_document(self.source_path)
        segments = split_document(doc, mode)
        project.create_project(pdir, name, self.source_path, mode, segments)
        self.EndModal(wx.ID_OK)

        # Open the recording window
        dlg = RecordingDialog(self.GetParent(), pdir, self.settings, self.store)
        dlg.ShowModal()

31.4 Key Takeaways

  • Modal dialogs block the parent — use for settings, wizards, confirmations
  • ShowModal() returns wx.ID_OK or wx.ID_CANCEL
  • Always call Destroy() on dialogs (or use with statement)
  • wx.adv.Wizard provides multi-step wizard pages with Next/Back/Finish
  • The AIVS wizard has 2 pages: Details (name, document, punctuation) and Mode (splitting method)

Custom Drawing & Device Context

32.1 Device Context (DC) Basics

import wx

class WaveformPanel(wx.Panel):
    """Custom panel that draws an audio waveform."""

    def __init__(self, parent):
        super().__init__(parent)
        self._samples = []
        self.Bind(wx.EVT_PAINT, self._on_paint)

    def set_samples(self, samples):
        self._samples = samples
        self.Refresh()  # Trigger repaint

    def _on_paint(self, event):
        dc = wx.PaintDC(self)
        width, height = self.GetSize()

        # Clear background
        dc.SetBackground(wx.Brush(wx.WHITE))
        dc.Clear()

        if not self._samples:
            return

        # Draw waveform
        dc.SetPen(wx.Pen(wx.BLUE, 1))
        mid = height // 2
        step = max(1, len(self._samples) // width)

        for x in range(width):
            idx = int(x * len(self._samples) / width)
            sample = self._samples[idx] / 32768.0
            y = int(mid - sample * mid * 0.9)
            dc.DrawPoint(x, y)

32.3 Themed Drawing in AIVS

# From gui/theme.py — applying colors to controls
def _paint(window: wx.Window, colors: dict) -> None:
    """Apply theme colors to a control."""
    try:
        if isinstance(window, (wx.Panel, wx.Dialog, wx.Frame)):
            window.SetBackgroundColour(colors["bg"])
        elif isinstance(window, (wx.StaticText, wx.CheckBox)):
            window.SetForegroundColour(colors["fg"])
        elif isinstance(window, (wx.TextCtrl, wx.ComboBox)):
            window.SetBackgroundColour(colors["control_bg"])
            window.SetForegroundColour(colors["control_fg"])
    except Exception:
        pass  # Some controls don't support color changes

32.4 Key Takeaways

  • DC (Device Context) is the drawing API — paint, draw, fill
  • BufferedDC prevents flicker by double-buffering
  • Bind(EVT_PAINT) for custom drawing; call Refresh() to trigger repaint
  • AIVS uses DC drawing for theme application across all widgets

Ch33 Threading Gui
Chapter 33

Threading in GUI Applications

Learning Objectives

  • Understand why threading + GUI requires special care
  • Master the wx.PostEvent pattern for thread-safe GUI updates
  • See the complete SynthesisWorker pattern in AIVS

33.1 The Rule: Never Touch GUI from Worker Threads

Rule #1: wxPython widgets are NOT thread-safe. You must NEVER call widget methods from a worker thread. Always use wx.PostEvent() to send messages to the main thread, where the GUI handler updates the widgets. 
# ❌ WRONG — crashes or corrupts GUI
def worker(self):
    self.status_label.SetLabel("Working...")  # DANGER!

# ✓ CORRECT — post event to main thread
def worker(self):
    wx.PostEvent(self, SynthStatusEvent("Working..."))

# ✓ CORRECT — use wx.CallAfter for simple cases
def worker(self):
    wx.CallAfter(self.status_label.SetLabel, "Working...")

33.2 The Complete Pattern

The AIVS Recording Dialog demonstrates the full pattern:

# 1. Define custom events
_SYNTH_STATUS = wx.NewEventType()
EVT_SYNTH_STATUS = wx.PyEventBinder(_SYNTH_STATUS, 1)

class SynthStatusEvent(wx.PyCommandEvent):
    def __init__(self, message: str):
        super().__init__(_SYNTH_STATUS)
        self.message = message

# 2. Create the worker thread
class SynthesisWorker(threading.Thread):
    def __init__(self, ..., on_status, on_segment_done, on_all_done, on_error):
        super().__init__(daemon=True)
        self._on_status = on_status
        self._on_done = on_segment_done
        self._on_all_done = on_all_done
        self._on_error = on_error

    def run(self):
        try:
            for i, seg in enumerate(self._segments):
                self._on_status(f"Recording {seg.title}...")
                # ... synthesize ...
                self._on_done(i, seg.title, path)
            self._on_all_done()
        except Exception as exc:
            self._on_error(str(exc))

# 3. Launch from GUI (main thread)
def _on_start(self, _):
    self._worker = SynthesisWorker(
        segments=self._segments,
        on_status=lambda msg: wx.PostEvent(self, SynthStatusEvent(msg)),
        on_segment_done=lambda i, t, p: wx.PostEvent(self, SynthSegmentDoneEvent(i, t, p)),
        on_all_done=lambda: wx.PostEvent(self, SynthFinishedEvent()),
        on_error=lambda msg: wx.PostEvent(self, SynthErrorEvent(msg)),
    )
    self._worker.start()

# 4. Handle events (main thread)
self.Bind(EVT_SYNTH_STATUS, self._on_synth_status)
self.Bind(EVT_SYNTH_SEGMENT_DONE, self._on_segment_done)
self.Bind(EVT_SYNTH_FINISHED, self._on_finished)
self.Bind(EVT_SYNTH_ERROR, self._on_error)

def _on_synth_status(self, evt):
    self.status_label.SetLabel(evt.message)  # Safe — main thread

33.3 Cancel and Pause Patterns

# Using threading.Event for cancellation
self._cancel_event = threading.Event()

# Worker checks periodically
def run(self):
    for seg in self._segments:
        if self._cancel_event.is_set():
            break  # Exit gracefully
        # ... process segment ...

# GUI signals cancellation
def _on_stop(self, _):
    self._cancel_event.set()
    self.status_label.SetLabel("Stopping...")

# Pause uses a separate event
self._pause_event = threading.Event()

def run(self):
    for seg in self._segments:
        while self._pause_event.is_set():
            if self._cancel_event.is_set():
                break
            time.sleep(0.1)  # Wait while paused
        # ... process segment ...

33.4 Key Takeaways

  • Never touch GUI widgets from worker threads
  • wx.PostEvent() sends events from worker → GUI safely
  • wx.CallAfter() is a simpler alternative for single calls
  • Use threading.Event for cancel/pause signaling
  • The AIVS pattern: Worker thread → custom wx events → GUI handlers

Ch34 Accessibility
Chapter 34

Accessibility (a11y)

Learning Objectives

  • Understand why accessibility matters in desktop apps
  • Make wxPython apps accessible with SetName() and proper labels
  • See the AIVS a11y helper system

34.1 What Is Accessibility?

Accessibility (a11y) ensures that people with disabilities can use your software. For a text-to-speech application like AIVS, this is especially important because many users rely on screen readers (NVDA, JAWS, Narrator).

34.2 wxPython Accessibility Basics

# Every control needs a readable name for screen readers
button = wx.Button(parent, label="Start recording")
button.SetName("Start recording")  # MSAA/UIA accessible name

# Text controls should be read-only and have clear names
text = wx.TextCtrl(
    parent,
    style=wx.TE_MULTILINE | wx.TE_READONLY,
    size=(-1, 130),
)
text.SetName("Text to record")
text.SetToolTip("Read-only preview of the text that will be synthesized")

# ComboBoxes need accessible names
combo = wx.ComboBox(parent, style=wx.CB_READONLY)
combo.SetName("Select TTS engine")

# Announce state changes
self.status = wx.StaticText(self, label="Ready.")
self.status.SetName("Recording status")
self.status.SetToolTip("Current status of the recording process")

34.3 AIVS a11y Helper

# From gui/a11y.py
def add_labeled(parent, sizer, label_text, control, **kwargs):
    """Add a label-control pair with screen reader support."""
    label = wx.StaticText(parent, label=label_text + ":")
    _tint(label)  # Apply theme colors
    sizer.Add(label, 0, wx.ALIGN_CENTER_VERTICAL | wx.ALL, 4)
    control.SetName(label_text)  # Set accessible name
    sizer.Add(control, 1, wx.EXPAND | wx.ALL, 4)
    return label

def add_check(parent, sizer, label_text, checked=False):
    """CheckBox with accessible name."""
    box = wx.CheckBox(parent, label=label_text)
    box.SetValue(checked)
    box.SetName(label_text)
    sizer.Add(box, 0, wx.ALL, 4)
    return box

def set_accessible_name(control, name):
    control.SetName(name)

34.4 Tab Order and Focus

# Tab order follows creation order in the sizer
# AIVS puts the text preview first so screen readers
# announce the content before the controls

# Announce page changes in wizards
def _on_page_changed(self, evt):
    page = evt.GetPage()
    if evt.GetDirection():  # Forward
        if page is self.page_details:
            self.page_details.name_ctrl.SetFocus()
    evt.Skip()

# Set initial focus when dialogs open
self.SetName(f"Recording: {project_name}")
wx.CallAfter(self.text_preview.SetFocus)

35.1 Theme Manager in AIVS

# From gui/theme.py
_LIGHT = {"bg": "#ffffff", "fg": "#1a1a1a",
          "control_bg": "#ffffff", "control_fg": "#1a1a1a"}
_DARK = {"bg": "#1e1e1e", "fg": "#e8e8e8",
         "control_bg": "#2d2d2d", "control_fg": "#e8e8e8"}

_state = {"theme": THEME_SYSTEM, "colors": _LIGHT}
_lock = threading.Lock()

def apply_theme(top: wx.Window, theme: str) -> None:
    """Apply theme to window and all descendants."""
    resolved = _resolve(theme)
    colors = _DARK if resolved == THEME_DARK else _LIGHT
    with _lock:
        _state["theme"] = theme
        _state["colors"] = colors
    _paint(top, colors)
    for child in _descendants(top):
        _paint(child, colors)
    top.Refresh()

def _resolve(theme: str) -> str:
    """Resolve 'system' to light or dark based on OS."""
    if theme == THEME_SYSTEM:
        try:
            appearance = wx.SystemSettings.GetAppearance()
            return THEME_DARK if appearance.IsDark() else THEME_LIGHT
        except Exception:
            return THEME_LIGHT
    return theme

35.2 Applying Colors to Widgets

def _paint(window: wx.Window, colors: dict) -> None:
    try:
        # Containers get background color
        if isinstance(window, (wx.Panel, wx.Dialog, wx.Frame, wx.ScrolledWindow)):
            window.SetBackgroundColour(colors["bg"])

        # Text labels get foreground color
        elif isinstance(window, (wx.StaticText, wx.CheckBox, wx.RadioButton)):
            window.SetForegroundColour(colors["fg"])

        # Input controls get both
        elif isinstance(window, (wx.TextCtrl, wx.ComboBox, wx.ListBox)):
            window.SetBackgroundColour(colors["control_bg"])
            window.SetForegroundColour(colors["control_fg"])
    except Exception:
        pass  # Some widgets don't support color changes

  • Three themes: Light, Dark, System (auto-detect OS preference)
  • wx.SystemSettings.GetAppearance() detects dark mode on Windows 10/11

from wx.adv import Wizard, WizardPage, EVT_WIZARD_FINISHED, EVT_WIZARD_PAGE_CHANGED

class NewProjectWizard(Wizard):
    def __init__(self, parent, settings, store):
        super().__init__(parent, title="New Project")

        # Create pages
        self.page_details = _DetailsPage(self)
        self.page_mode = _ModePage(self, settings)

        # Wire up the page area
        self.GetPageAreaSizer().Add(self.page_details)

        # Events
        self.Bind(EVT_WIZARD_FINISHED, self._on_finish)
        self.Bind(EVT_WIZARD_PAGE_CHANGED, self._on_page_changed)

class _DetailsPage(WizardPage):
    def __init__(self, wizard):
        super().__init__(wizard)
        self.wizard = wizard
        self._build_ui()

    def GetNext(self):
        return self.wizard.page_mode  # Next page

    def GetPrev(self):
        return None  # This is the first page

37.2 Audio Operations in AIVS

# From tts/engine.py — pitch shifting
def _shift_pitch(samples: np.ndarray, pitch: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Shift pitch without changing duration (resample)."""
    if pitch == 1.0:
        return samples
    # Resample to change pitch
    new_length = int(len(samples) / pitch)
    indices = np.linspace(0, len(samples) - 1, new_length)
    shifted = np.interp(indices, np.arange(len(samples)), samples.astype(np.float64))
    return shifted.astype(np.int16)

# From tts/engine.py — volume adjustment
def _apply_volume(samples: np.ndarray, volume: float) -> np.ndarray:
    """Scale audio samples by volume factor."""
    if volume == 1.0:
        return samples
    scaled = samples.astype(np.float64) * volume
    return np.clip(scaled, -32768, 32767).astype(np.int16)

# From clone/worker.py — base64 encode/decode for IPC
# Worker → App: encode audio as base64
samples_int16 = np.clip(arr, -1.0, 1.0) * 32767.0
wav_b64 = base64.b64encode(samples_int16.astype(np.int16).tobytes()).decode("ascii")

# App → decode from base64
raw = base64.b64decode(resp["wav"])
samples = np.frombuffer(raw, dtype=np.int16).copy()

37.3 WAV File Writing

import wave

def write_wav(path: str, samples: np.ndarray, sample_rate: int = 24000):
    """Write int16 samples to a WAV file."""
    with wave.open(path, "wb") as wf:
        wf.setnchannels(1)       # Mono
        wf.setsampwidth(2)       # 16-bit = 2 bytes
        wf.setframerate(sample_rate)
        wf.writeframes(samples.tobytes())

38.2 AIVS Model Downloader

# From tts/downloader.py
def _download_file(url, dest, progress=None, cancel_event=None):
    """Download a file with progress and cancellation."""
    with requests.get(url, stream=True, timeout=60) as resp:
        resp.raise_for_status()
        total = int(resp.headers.get("content-length", 0))
        downloaded = 0
        with open(dest, "wb") as f:
            for chunk in resp.iter_content(chunk_size=65536):
                if cancel_event and cancel_event.is_set():
                    raise DownloadCancelled()
                f.write(chunk)
                downloaded += len(chunk)
                if progress:
                    progress("downloading", downloaded, total)

Ch39 Sherpa Onnx
Chapter 39

sherpa-onnx TTS Engine

Learning Objectives

  • Understand sherpa-onnx's role in AIVS
  • Configure and use the TTS engine
  • See how multiple TTS engines are supported

39.1 What Is sherpa-onnx?

sherpa-onnx is a C++ speech processing library with Python bindings, using the ONNX runtime for inference. It supports multiple TTS model formats:

  • VITS — used by Piper voices
  • Kokoro — multi-speaker multi-language
  • Matcha — flow-matching TTS with vocoder
  • Kitten — small efficient models

39.2 TTS Engine Wrapper in AIVS

# From tts/engine.py — simplified
import sherpa_onnx
import numpy as np

class TtsEngine:
    """Wrapper around sherpa-onnx TTS."""
    sample_rate = 24000

    def __init__(self, voice_entry: dict):
        files = resolve_voice_files(voice_entry)
        config = sherpa_onnx.OfflineTtsConfig(
            model=sherpa_onnx.OfflineTtsModelConfig(
                vits=sherpa_onnx.OfflineTtsVitsModelConfig(
                    model=files["model"],
                    tokens=files["tokens"],
                    data_dir=files.get("data_dir", ""),
                    lexicon=files.get("lexicon", ""),
                    dict_dir=files.get("dict_dir", ""),
                ),
                num_threads=1,
            ),
            max_num_sentences=1,
        )
        self._tts = sherpa_onnx.OfflineTts(config)

    def synthesize(self, text, sid=0, speed=1.0, pitch=1.0, volume=1.0):
        if not text.strip():
            raise ValueError("Nothing to synthesize")

        # Core synthesis
        audio = self._tts.generate(text=text, sid=sid, speed=speed)
        samples = np.array(audio.samples, dtype=np.int16)

        # Apply post-processing
        if pitch != 1.0:
            samples = _shift_pitch(samples, pitch)
        if volume != 1.0:
            samples = _apply_volume(samples, volume)

        return samples

# Engine caching (one engine per voice)
_engine_cache: dict[str, TtsEngine] = {}

def get_engine(voice_entry: dict) -> TtsEngine:
    """Get or create a cached engine."""
    key = voice_entry.get("voice", "")
    if key not in _engine_cache:
        _engine_cache[key] = TtsEngine(voice_entry)
    return _engine_cache[key]

    for row in table.rows:

40.3 AIVS Document Parser

# From documents/parsers.py
class ParseError(Exception):
    """Raised when a document cannot be parsed."""

def parse_document(path: str) -> Document:
    """Parse a document and return structured content."""
    ext = os.path.splitext(path)[1].lower()
    if ext == ".pdf":
        return _parse_pdf(path)
    elif ext == ".docx":
        return _parse_docx(path)
    elif ext in (".txt", ".md"):
        return _parse_text(path)
    elif ext in (".html", ".htm"):
        return _parse_html(path)
    else:
        raise ParseError(f"Unsupported file type: {ext}")

class Document:
    """Parsed document with blocks of text."""
    def __init__(self):
        self.blocks: list[TextBlock] = []
        self.metadata: dict = {}

class TextBlock:
    """A section of text with a heading and content."""
    def __init__(self, heading: str, text: str, level: int = 0):
        self.heading = heading
        self.text = text
        self.level = level

41.2 AIVS FFmpeg Management

# From audio/ffmpeg.py
def ensure_ffmpeg() -> str | None:
    """Find or return None if FFmpeg is not installed."""
    ffmpeg_path = os.path.join(paths.user_data_dir(), "ffmpeg", "ffmpeg.exe")
    if os.path.isfile(ffmpeg_path):
        return ffmpeg_path
    return None

def convert_wav(input_path, output_path, format, ffmpeg_exe):
    """Convert WAV to MP3 or FLAC using FFmpeg."""
    import subprocess
    cmd = [ffmpeg_exe, "-i", input_path, "-y", output_path]
    subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, check=True)

# Usage in RecordingDialog
if fmt != "wav":
    ffmpeg_exe = ffmpeg_mod.ensure_ffmpeg()
    if not ffmpeg_exe:
        # Offer to download FFmpeg
        answer = wx.MessageBox(
            "FFmpeg is required for MP3/FLAC. Download now?",
            "FFmpeg required",
            style=wx.YES_NO | wx.ICON_QUESTION,
        )
        if answer == wx.YES:
            ffmpeg_mod.download_ffmpeg()

42.1 Why Virtual Environments?

Without venvs, installing wxPython for one project might overwrite a package needed by another. Virtual environments create isolated Python installations: 

# Create
python -m venv .venv

# Activate (Windows)
.venv\Scripts\activate

# Activate (macOS/Linux)
source .venv/bin/activate

# Install packages (only in this venv)
pip install wxPython numpy sherpa-onnx

# Deactivate
deactivate

42.2 AIVS PythonRuntime

# From python_runtime/__init__.py
class PythonRuntime:
    """Manages a separate Python venv for addons and optional engines."""

    def __init__(self, env_dir=None):
        self._env_dir = env_dir or os.path.join(
            paths.user_data_dir(), "addon_env"
        )

    def ensure_env(self) -> str:
        """Create the venv if it doesn't exist."""
        if self.is_created:
            return self._env_dir
        subprocess.run(
            [self.system_python, "-m", "venv", self._env_dir, "--clear"],
            check=True,
        )
        return self._env_dir

    def pip_install(self, packages, progress=None, cancel_event=None):
        """Install packages into the managed venv."""
        pip = self.ensure_pip()
        cmd = [pip, "install", "--no-warn-script-location"] + packages
        proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, text=True)
        for line in proc.stdout:
            if progress:
                progress(line, 0, 0)
            if cancel_event and cancel_event.is_set():
                proc.terminate()
                return {"ok": False, "error": "Cancelled"}
        proc.wait()
        return {"ok": proc.returncode == 0}

    def run_in_env(self, script: str):
        """Run a Python script inside the managed venv."""
        return subprocess.run(
            [self.python_exe, "-c", script],
            capture_output=True, text=True,
        )

42.3 Key Takeaways

  • Virtual environments isolate project dependencies
  • AIVS has two venvs: the development venv (requirements.txt) and the managed addon venv
  • The PythonRuntime manages the addon venv for pip-installed engines (OmniVoice)
  • run_in_env() executes scripts inside the managed venv without affecting the main process

43.4 Key Takeaways

  • AIVS has 53 Python source files across 13 subpackages
  • The architecture follows layered design: GUI → Business Logic → TTS Engine → Infrastructure
  • Heavy TTS engines run in separate subprocesses (Clone, OmniVoice)
  • The data flow is: Document → Parser → Splitter → Project → Recording → Audio
  • JSON is the universal data format (settings, projects, catalog, worker protocol)
